claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a white console with the circular 'X' logo and perforated grill characteristic of the Xbox One S.
Photo 0 explicitly shows a disc drive slot visible on the front, which is absent on the All-Digital Edition.
Photo 1 shows the unit being held in a hand, confirming the slim/compact form factor.

risks.risk: Internal storage capacity is unknown (500GB vs 1TB).
risks.proof: A screenshot of the 'Settings > System > Storage' screen.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty (especially given the seller's 'disc-free' claim).
risks.proof: A video showing a game disc being inserted, recognized, and launched.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive.

risks.risk: The console may be banned from Xbox Network.
risks.proof: A video showing the console successfully signed into an Xbox profile and accessing the Microsoft Store.

risks.risk: The HDMI port or internal APU may be damaged (no video output).
risks.proof: A video of the console booting up to the home dashboard on a TV screen.

risks.risk: Hidden physical damage or overheating issues under the plastic wrap.
risks.proof: Photos of the console with the plastic wrap removed and a video of it running a game for 10 minutes.
risks.if_unproven: as 'fair' condition with potential thermal issues.

proof_requests: Video of the console powered on and displaying the dashboard on a TV.
Screenshot of the 'Storage' settings showing total capacity.
Video of a disc being inserted and read by the console.
Photos of the console without the clear plastic wrap.
Photos of the rear ports to check for damage.
response.reason: The witness confirms the item is an Xbox One S, though the seller's 'All-Digital' claim is contradicted by the visible disc slot. It can be priced at the worst-case value for a 500GB unit with a broken drive and no accessories.
